subject: economics

concepts.title: Net Investment and Depreciation
concepts.definition: Net investment measures the real expansion of capital stock after accounting for physical degradation and usage loss of existing capital equipment.
concepts.key_idea: Capital accumulation increases only when total gross capital formation exceeds asset depreciation.
question_patterns: find the net investment given gross investment and depreciation
calculate net capital formation when gross investment and wear and tear are known
determine net investment from gross investment and depreciation
compute net investment given gross capital expenditure and depreciation allowance
what is the value of net investment if gross investment and annual depreciation are given

solution_steps.explain: net capital formation is obtained by subtracting asset wear and tear from gross investment

concepts.title: Gross Value Added Method
concepts.definition: Value added measures the fresh contribution made by an enterprise to production by deducting intermediate consumption from total gross production value.
concepts.key_idea: Subtracting intermediate input costs eliminates double counting of goods across successive production stages.
question_patterns: calculate gross value added given sales intermediate consumption and inventory change
find the net contribution of a firm using sales stock change and intermediate costs
determine gross value added from total output value and intermediate goods value
compute gross value added when sales intermediate consumption and inventory change are provided
what is the gross value added for a firm given sales and intermediate inputs

solution_steps.explain: gross output value combines total market sales with net inventory change
gross value added is found by deducting intermediate goods expenditure from gross output

concepts.title: Expenditure Approach to GDP
concepts.definition: The expenditure method measures national output by aggregating total final spending on goods and services by households, business investors, government, and foreign trade.
concepts.formula: gdp = consumption + investment + govt_expenditure + exports - imports
concepts.key_idea: Aggregate spending across economic sectors equals total final domestic product.
question_patterns: calculate gross domestic product using the expenditure method
find gdp from private consumption investment government spending exports and imports
determine aggregate expenditure given consumption investment government purchases and net exports
compute GDP when aggregate consumption investment government spending and net exports are given
what is the GDP calculated via spending by households firms government and foreign trade

solution_steps.explain: net exports represent total foreign sales minus foreign purchases
add final consumption, investment, government spending, and net exports to compute GDP

concepts.title: Income Approach to GDP
concepts.definition: The income method sums primary factor rewards earned by households for offering labor, capital, land, and entrepreneurship to production activities.
concepts.key_idea: Production revenue is entirely distributed to domestic factors of production as factor income payments.
question_patterns: calculate gross domestic product using the income method
find GDP from wages profits interest and rent payments
determine total factor payments from wage bill profit income interest and rental yields
compute aggregate income given wages profits interest and rent
what is the GDP evaluated as the sum of all factor incomes in the economy

solution_steps.explain: add wage payments, corporate profits, net interest earnings, and land rents to arrive at GDP

concepts.title: GVA and GDP at Factor Cost Basic Prices and Market Prices
concepts.definition: Production costs transition to basic prices by adding net production taxes, and further transition to market prices by adding net product taxes.
concepts.formula: gdp_market_price = gva_factor_cost + production_taxes - production_subsidies + product_taxes - product_subsidies
concepts.key_idea: Government tax claims and financial subsidies cause differences between output factor costs and final market prices.
question_patterns: calculate GDP at market prices from GVA at factor cost and net taxes
find GVA at basic prices given factor cost and net production taxes
determine market price GDP from basic price GVA and net product taxes
compute GDP at market price when factor cost net production tax and net product tax are known
what is the GDP at market prices given GVA at factor cost production taxes subsidies and product taxes

solution_steps.explain: add net production taxes (production taxes minus production subsidies) to factor cost GVA
add net product taxes (product taxes minus product subsidies) to GVA at basic prices

concepts.title: Gross National Product and Net National Product
concepts.definition: Gross National Product accounts for net factor income earned abroad by residents, while Net National Product deducts capital consumption allowances.
concepts.key_idea: National aggregates measure economic earnings owned by residents, independent of geographical production locations.
question_patterns: calculate GNP at market price given GDP and net factor income from abroad
find NNP at market price from GDP net factor income and depreciation
determine net national product at market prices given gross domestic product foreign income and depreciation
compute GNP and NNP when GDP net factor income from abroad and depreciation are known
what is NNP at market price given GDP NFIA and capital consumption

solution_steps.explain: add net factor income from abroad to gross domestic product at market price
deduct annual capital depreciation from gross national product at market price

concepts.title: National Income and Personal Income
concepts.definition: National Income is net national product at factor cost, whereas Personal Income captures actual money receipts accruing to private household units.
concepts.formula: personal_income = national_income - undistributed_profits - corporate_tax - net_interest_paid + transfer_payments
concepts.key_idea: Personal income modifies national income by subtracting retained corporate earnings and direct business taxes while adding social transfers.
question_patterns: calculate personal income from national income corporate tax undistributed profits and transfer payments
find national income from NNP at market price and net indirect taxes
determine personal income given national income retained profits corporate tax net interest and transfers
compute personal income when national income corporate tax undistributed profit and transfers are known
what is personal income calculated from national factor earnings and transfer receipts

solution_steps.explain: subtract undistributed profits, corporate tax, and net household interest from national income, then add transfer payments
solution_steps.compute: personal_income = national_income - undistributed_profits - corporate_tax - net_interest_paid + transfer_payments

concepts.title: Personal Disposable Income
concepts.definition: Personal Disposable Income represents net spendable earnings left with households after paying personal income taxes and mandatory government fees.
concepts.key_idea: Household consumption and private savings depend directly on personal disposable income.
question_patterns: calculate personal disposable income given personal income personal tax and non tax payments
find disposable income of households after direct tax payments and fines
determine spendable household income from personal income direct taxes and fee payments
compute personal disposable income when personal income personal taxes and non tax payments are known
what is personal disposable income if income tax and statutory non tax fees are deducted from personal income

solution_steps.explain: subtract personal taxes and non-tax administrative fees from personal income to obtain personal disposable income

concepts.title: Nominal GDP Real GDP and GDP Deflator
concepts.definition: The GDP deflator measures broad price inflation by calculating the numerical ratio of current-price nominal GDP to base-price real GDP.
concepts.key_idea: Real GDP isolates physical volume changes, while nominal GDP reflects both output quantity changes and price movements.
question_patterns: calculate GDP deflator from nominal GDP and real GDP
find real GDP given nominal GDP and GDP deflator
determine price index or GDP deflator in percentage terms
compute GDP deflator when nominal output and real output are given
what is the implicit price deflator given nominal and real output figures

solution_steps.explain: divide nominal GDP by real GDP and scale by 100 to obtain the GDP deflator index percentage

concepts.title: Consumer Price Index Calculation
concepts.definition: The Consumer Price Index evaluates retail cost changes for a fixed consumer basket in the current period relative to a specified base period.
concepts.key_idea: CPI measures retail price changes impacting household consumption spending using fixed basket weights.
question_patterns: calculate consumer price index given base year cost and current year cost
find CPI for current year relative to base year basket expenditure
determine percentage change in consumer basket cost using CPI
compute consumer price index when base cost and current cost are given
what is the CPI given basket costs in base and current periods

solution_steps.action: compute price ratio relative to base period
solution_steps.explain: divide current year basket expenditure by base year basket expenditure and multiply by 100

concepts.title: Limitations of GDP as a Welfare Indicator
concepts.definition: Gross Domestic Product fails as a complete index of aggregate human welfare because it ignores income distribution, non-monetary work, and environmental impacts.
concepts.key_idea: Higher aggregate production figures do not automatically reflect an improvement in general social welfare.
question_patterns: explain why GDP may not reflect true economic welfare
what are the main limitations of using real GDP as a welfare measure
how do non monetary exchanges affect the estimation of GDP and welfare
discuss negative externalities and their impact on national welfare measurement
why does income distribution prevent GDP from serving as an ideal welfare index

solution_steps.explain: if increased aggregate income accrues mainly to top earners, overall standard of living for most citizens may fall
unpaid domestic labor and barter transactions create unrecorded productive value omitted from official GDP figures
unpriced industrial pollution degrades societal welfare without lowering recorded GDP totals
